newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SECOND SUCCESSIVE 66 PUTS MORGAN IN LEAD AT THE TRADITION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SECOND SUCCESSIVE 66 PUTS MORGAN IN LEAD AT THE TRADITION.

text.p: Gil Morgan fired his second successive six-under-par 66 to gain sole possession of the lead Friday after the second round of The Tradition, the Senior Tour's first major tournament of the year.
Morgan had been part of a five-way tie for the lead after Thursday's opening round, but his 66 was best round of the day Friday ang gave him a two-stroke lead.
Tied for second place at 10-under-par 134 were John Jacobs, Terry Dill and Isao Aoki of Japan.
Jim Dent, J.C. Snead and Graham Marsh of Australia were tied for fifth at seven-under 137.
Defending champion Jack Nicklaus, a four-time winner of this event and designer of the Cochise course on which it is played, struggled to a two-over 74 and fell nine shots off the pace at 141.

The 50-year-old Morgan joined the Senior Tour last September and won the Ralphs Senior Classic one week later. He is still looking for his first win this year, but is fifth on the 1997 money list with second and third-place finishes.
Nicklaus wasn't the only big name who had trouble Friday.
Raymond Floyd, who won this event in 1994, posted a 75 to fall to even par.

Jim Colbert, the 1995 and 1996 Senior Tour Player of the Year, and David Graham, the 1997 money leader, posted 74s and stood 14 shots back at 146. Graham is coming off a victory at last week's Dominion.
First prize in the $1.2 million tournament is $180,000.
